rows.item: i2c3 address collision
rows.measurement: 4 addressable devices on i2c3, 4 distinct addresses, 0 collisions: U2 TLV320AIC3104 @ 0x18, U11 BMI088 accelerometer @ 0x19, ToF module on Stemma J5 @ 0x29, U11 BMI088 gyroscope @ 0x68

rows.item: how close the bus came to colliding
rows.measurement: R14 is a 0 R link from +3V3 to U11.15 (SDO1). The BMI088 accelerometer defaults to 0x18 with SDO1 grounded — the SAME address as the TLV320AIC3104, which has no address pin and cannot move. R14 is the only thing keeping the two apart. Fit R14 to GND instead and the bus has two devices at 0x18.
rows.cite: copper: R14 [0R] pads {1: +3V3, 2: Net-(U11-SDO1)}; R15 [0R] pads {1: GND, 2: Net-(U11-SDO2)}

rows.item: every other I2C address in the robot
rows.measurement: IMX219 @ 0x10 is on I2C2 (the MIPI CSI connector pins 20/21), a DIFFERENT CONTROLLER from i2c3, so it cannot collide. U4 CAT24C32 @ 0x50 would sit on ID_SD/ID_SC (header 27/28 = I2C4_M0) but is DNP and its pull-ups R10/R11 are DNP too, so nothing is on that bus at all. The ET7301B USB-C PD controller answers at 0x22 on the RK3566 i2c3 controller in its M1 pin mux; Pollen re-muxes the controller to M0 and disables that node, so it is off the bus by pin mux, not by address.
rows.cite: part:imx219 i2c_address; HAT BOM DNP lines; teardown §4 "⚠ A trap they hit themselves"; part:radxa-zero-3w buses_the_microduck_uses.usb_c_pd_controller

rows.item: I2S master clock (pin 13)
rows.measurement: Header pin 13 = 'unconnected-(J4-Pin_13-Pad13)' — THE HAT DOES NOT CONNECT IT. The codec's MCLK (U2.1) is driven by Y1 [12 MHz], a 4-pad oscillator on the HAT with pins 1 and 4 on +3V3 and pin 2 on GND. So the Radxa supplies no master clock and needs no I2S3_MCLK_M0 pin. This is what the "fixed-clock" node in Pollen's audio overlay describes.
rows.cite: copper: J4 pad 13 net, Y1 pads; teardown §5b "Audio clocks: 12 MHz fixed MCLK"

rows.item: which I2S3 mux the HAT forces
rows.measurement: M0. The HAT wires I2S only to header pins 12/35/38/40, which are I2S3_*_M0. The M1 alternates sit on pins 19/21/23/24 — and those four pins are wired to the Stemma headers J7/J8 on this board, so M1 is not merely unused, it is OCCUPIED. This settles the open question in part:radxa-zero-3w unknowns[4] and in part:microduck-robot-hat-pcb uncertainties[3], where M0 was recorded as the wiring lane's ASSERTION. It is now a measurement.

rows.item: is any 5 V logic presented to a 3.3 V pin
rows.measurement: The only +5V pads that touch the header are J4.2 and J4.4, which are the Radxa's 5 V INPUT pins. Every signal pin the HAT drives (I2C, UART, I2S, INT1, the battery sense) is referenced to +3V3 or clamped: the battery sense is R24 10 k from +BATT with D2, a 3V3 zener, to GND, so header pin 31 sees 3.3 V and not 8.2 V. The Radxa's own limit is 3.63 V on all GPIOs.

rows.item: XL330-M288-T x15 on +BATT
rows.measurement: The copper puts the servo VDD on +BATT with nothing between: J13.2, J14.2, J3.2 and J11.2 are all +BATT, and no regulator on this board has +BATT on an output. The pack window under load is 6.6-8.2 V; the servo is rated 3.7-6.0 V, recommended 5.0 V. THE SERVOS RUN 0.6 V TO 2.2 V ABOVE THEIR RATED MAXIMUM AT ALL TIMES — 10.0 % over when the pack is empty, 36.7 % over when it is full. There is no operating point in the pack's range at which they are in spec.
rows.cite: ROBOTIS e-Manual XL330-M288-T Specifications: 'Operating Voltage 3.7 ~ 6.0 [V] (Recommended : 5.0 [V])'; local copy ce-parts/xl330-m288-t/iterations/v0.0.1/docs/fetched/robotis-emanual-xl330-m288.html | part:np-f550; Pollen's runtime maps 6.6 V (empty) to 8.2 V (full) UNDER LOAD, read through the servos' Present Input Voltage(144). out/open/power-battery.json sony_original_np_f550 + cell_class block. | copper: +BATT pad list

rows.item: how the reference robot survives that
rows.measurement: Pollen writes Shutdown(63) = 52 into every servo at boot. The vendor default is 53; 53 - 52 = 1 = bit 0, which is the Input Voltage Error bit. So the runtime CLEARS the servo's own over-voltage shutdown and leaves the overload and over-temperature bits armed. That is a fact about Pollen's code, not a vendor statement that 8.2 V is safe. ROBOTIS publishes no absolute maximum for this actuator, and the firmware's own Max Voltage Limit(32) cannot be set above 7.0 V — below the pack's own top. WHAT SETTLES IT: a meter on a servo VDD pin of a running robot, and a ROBOTIS statement of the absolute maximum.
rows.cite: research/raw/microduck_main_docs_design_robotd-design.md:253-257 (model.rs asserts return_delay_time=0, baud_rate=3, pwm_slope=255, shutdown=52); ce-parts/xl330-m288-t/iterations/v0.0.1/docs/DATASHEET.md §4 item 1

rows.item: the HAT itself on that same pack
rows.measurement: The HAT's own input range is 5-28 V (its README) and its buck accepts 3.8-32 V. The pack's 6.6-8.2 V is inside both. The board is fine on this pack; only the actuators sharing the same net are not. This is why the contradiction is easy to miss: the board is a general-purpose HAT rated far above what an XL330 will take, and the motor connector is both its power inlet and their supply.
rows.cite: reference/pollen-elec-rpi-robot-hat/README.md: 'can be power from 5 to 28V'; AP63205 DS41326 Rev 2-2 p.1

rows.item: ToF module IOVDD, if a VL53L8CX is fitted
rows.measurement: Stemma J5 offers +3V3 on pin 2 and 3.3 V logic (R12/R13 pull the bus to +3V3). part:vl53l5cx takes 3.0-3.6 V on both AVDD and IOVDD, so an L5CX is fine. part:vl53l8cx HAS NO 3.3 V IOVDD CONFIGURATION AT ALL — its IOVDD bands are 1.2 V and 1.8 V and its absolute maximum IOVDD is 1.98 V. Pollen's firmware supports both parts. So an L8CX can only be on this connector as a MODULE carrying its own 1.8 V regulator and level shifting; the bare chip on J5 would be 1.32 V over its absolute maximum. Which module is fitted is CANNOT DETERMINE. WHAT SETTLES IT: the part number on the ToF breakout in a teardown photo.
rows.cite: ce-parts/vl53l8cx/.../electrical.chip.json supplies[IOVDD] Table 12 p.20 and absolute_max Table 11; ce-parts/vl53l5cx/.../supplies[IOVDD] Table 12 p.17; teardown §7 "VL53L5CX or VL53L8CX"

rows.item: +BATT — servo demand under the walking policy
rows.measurement: Pack current from the servos: mean 1.2102 A, peak 2.0561 A over 2301 physics frames of the vx 0.25 m/s cell; worst single servo 1.2168 A (left_knee). Servo electrical power mean 8.9553 W, peak 15.2154 W. This is what the pack must deliver while walking.
rows.cite: out/sim-evidence/battery-runtime.json outputs.modes.walking; I = |tau|/kT per 200 Hz physics frame from out/sim-evidence/gait-torque-duty.json, kT from the XL330 stall rows

rows.item: +BATT — the number the budget is NOT sized for
rows.measurement: 15 servos all stalled at the 6.0 V row would be 26.10 A, and the pack, the wire and the connector would all be far past their ratings. The walking peak is 2.0561 A, 4.4 % of that. Nothing in the fetched material states a pack discharge limit, a connector rating for the fitted JST EH parts, or the XL330's current at any torque between 0 and stall — ROBOTIS publishes only the 17 mA standby and the three stall rows. So the margin between "walking" and "the wire melts" is UNMEASURED. WHAT SETTLES IT: a clamp meter on the pack lead through a fall-and-recover cycle, which is the load case the gait sweep does not cover.
rows.cite: XL330 stall rows (ROBOTIS e-Manual Specifications); out/sim-evidence/gait-peaks.json inputs.servo.note

rows.item: +BATT — everything is on ONE connector contact
rows.measurement: The battery enters on a motor connector (README, and the copper: no other +BATT terminal exists). J13 and J14 are wired in parallel — J13.1/J14.1 both GND, J13.2/J14.2 both +BATT, J13.3/J14.3 the same data net — so the pack current AND the whole servo chain's 2.0561 A peak AND the buck's input current pass through a single JST EH 2.5 mm contact pair. The fitted connector's current rating is not in any document fetched here. WHAT SETTLES IT: the JST EH series datasheet current rating, against the measured peak.
rows.cite: copper: J13/J14 pad->net table; reference/pollen-elec-rpi-robot-hat/README.md

rows.item: +5V — what is on it
rows.measurement: 19 pads: the Radxa (J4.2, J4.4), the amplifier U1 (pins 4 and 13, plus FB1 to its VDD), three 0 R straps R3/R4/R5 that hold PAM8406 ~SHDN, ~MUTE and MODE high, two 10 k mic-bias resistors R22/R23 to the Wago mic terminals, R8 100 R to the LM5050 sense pin, and the ideal-diode FET Q2. Source limit 2.0 A.
rows.cite: copper; AP63205 DS41326 Rev 2-2 p.1 "2A Continuous Output Current"

rows.item: +5V — does 2 A cover the Radxa plus the amplifier
rows.measurement: Radxa states a 5 V / 2 A adapter for the ZERO 3W and publishes NO board current figure anywhere in the four documents fetched (product brief, wiki, two schematics) — part:radxa-zero-3w unknowns[1] says so. The PAM8406D publishes output POWER, not supply current: 3.14 W per channel into 4 ohm at THD+N 10 %, VDD 5 V, with efficiency up to 90 %. Only ONE channel leaves the board — the copper shows the RIGHT channel going through FB2/FB3 to the Wago speaker terminal J1, while the LEFT channel's two outputs terminate at test points TP3 and TP4 and nothing else — so the amplifier bound is one channel, about 3.14/0.90 = 3.49 W = 0.70 A at 5 V, not two channels. The buck can give 2.00 A total. If the Radxa ever draws its stated 2 A adapter rating while audio is playing, the rail is over-subscribed by roughly 0.70 A. It CANNOT BE GRADED without a board-current measurement. WHAT SETTLES IT: a meter in series with header pin 2 while the policy runs and the speaker plays.
rows.cite: part:radxa-zero-3w power[0] cite (brief §5.1 p.5) and unknowns[1]; 'part - PAM8406 - C86270.pdf' PO table and 'Efficiency up to 90% with Class-D Mode'; copper: U1.1/U1.3 -> TP3/TP4 only, U1.16/U1.14 -> FB3/FB2 -> J1

rows.item: +3V3 — demand versus a supply nobody has stated
rows.measurement: 55 pads on +3V3, and the rail is SOURCED BY THE RADXA through header pins 1 and 17 — the HAT makes no 3.3 V. Known demand: U2 7.35 mA, U11 5.15 mA, ToF module on J5 95 mA typical / 150 mA peak = 107.50 mA typical, 162.50 mA with the ToF at its peak. NOT COUNTED because no figure was transcribed: U8, U3, MK1, the four Stemma headers J5-J8 (anything a user plugs in), and Y1 the 12 MHz oscillator. THE SUPPLY SIDE IS THE PROBLEM: no fetched Radxa document states how much current the 40-pin 3.3 V pins can deliver, and the RK817 PMIC rail behind them is not broken out per-rail in the brief. A 145 mA peak demand on an unstated supply is not a pass. WHAT SETTLES IT: the RK817 datasheet LDO rating for the rail that feeds header pins 1/17, or a meter.
rows.cite: copper +3V3 pad list; per-device cites in DEVICE_FACTS; part:radxa-zero-3w power[4] "Board-level current draw: NOT stated in any fetched document"

rows.item: the whole chain, pack to peak, and the ONE number that is missing
rows.measurement: Pack -> +BATT: the 15 servos take a measured 2.0561 A peak / 1.2102 A mean while walking. Pack -> U9 -> +5V -> the Radxa and the amplifier: 5.000 V at up to 2.000 A = 10.0 W, and reflected to the pack at its EMPTY voltage of 6.6 V that is P/(eta x 6.6) — 0.4785 A to 0.5682 A per 3 W at an efficiency of 0.95 to 0.80 (the AP63205 efficiency curve was NOT transcribed, so the band is stated, not a number). Everything on that path is measured or bounded EXCEPT ONE THING: the Radxa Zero 3W board current, which no fetched Radxa document states in any operating condition. It is the single number that closes this budget. The runtime table already sweeps it: 1.0 W gives 113 min of walking and 5.0 W gives 80 min. WHAT SETTLES IT: an ammeter in series with header pin 2 while the policy runs.
rows.cite: out/sim-evidence/battery-runtime.json outputs.runtime_table.walking; AP63205 DS41326 Rev 2-2 p.1; part:radxa-zero-3w unknowns[1]

rows.item: the press kit's ~1 h needs more compute power than the buck can deliver
rows.measurement: Pollen publish ~1 h on an 18.7 Wh pack, i.e. 18.7 W average. This lane measures the servos at 8.9553 W while walking, which leaves 9.7447 W for everything else. THE HAT'S BUCK CANNOT DELIVER THAT: the AP63205 is a fixed-5.0 V part rated 2 A, so 10.0 W is its whole output, and 9.7447 W is 97.4 % of it with nothing left for the audio amplifier. The battery-runtime study reached the same conclusion from the RADXA'S adapter rating; this is an independent second reason, from the HAT side, and it means the press-kit hour is NOT an hour of compute-heavy walking on this hardware. The missing power is on the servo side, where the XL330's no-load current is unpublished and fifteen of them multiply it.
rows.cite: out/sim-evidence/battery-runtime.json outputs.pollen_claim; AP63205 DS41326 Rev 2-2 p.1 "2A Continuous Output Current"

rows.item: +1V8 — demand versus the LDO
rows.measurement: 4 pads: U3.2 (the LDO output), U2.32 (the codec DVDD) and two capacitors. The only load is the codec digital core, 2.45 mA at its worst printed row, against the XC6206's 100 mA IOUT(max) at VIN = VOUT + 1 V — and here VIN is 3.3 V, 1.5 V of headroom. 2.5 % of the LDO. This is the one rail in the robot whose budget closes with numbers on both sides.
rows.cite: copper; SLAS510G p.12 IDVDD rows; 'part - XC6202 - C347373.pdf' IOUT(max) row

rows.cite: wiring/cables.json record.cables

rows.item: run tof-hat lands on J5
rows.measurement: tof <-> HAT. The copper's connector is J5 (JST SH 4-pin), footprint Connector_JST:JST_SH_BM04B-SRSS-TB_1x04-1MP_P1.00mm_Vertical. Modelled pins: GND, 3V3, SDA, SCL (I2C3, addr 0x29)
rows.cite: copper; wiring/cables.json

rows.item: run spk-hat lands on J1
rows.measurement: speaker <-> HAT. The copper's connector is J1 (Wago-2 screwless terminal), footprint LCSC_parts_lib:Wago_2059-302_998-403. Modelled pins: SPK+, SPK- (codec line/HP out, or an amplifier: CANNOT DETERMINE)
rows.cite: copper; wiring/cables.json

rows.item: run mic-hat lands on J2 or J9
rows.measurement: mic <-> HAT. The copper's connector is J2 or J9 (Wago-2 screwless terminal), footprint LCSC_parts_lib:Wago_2059-302_998-403. Modelled pins: MIC, BIAS, GND (codec Mic3R, community)
rows.cite: copper; wiring/cables.json

rows.item: run bat-hat lands on a Dynamixel motor connector
rows.measurement: battery <-> HAT. The copper's connector is a Dynamixel motor connector (JST EH — THERE IS NO BATTERY TERMINAL). Modelled pins: BAT+, BAT- (via the banana contact PCB)
rows.cite: copper; wiring/cables.json

rows.item: run hat-radxa-40pin lands on J4
rows.measurement: radxa <-> HAT. The copper's connector is J4 (2x20 SMD female header), footprint Library_Pollen:PinHeader_2x20_P2.54mm_Vertical_with_rasp_HAT_zero_SMD_connector. Modelled pins: 40-pin header: 5 V (pins 2/4), GND, UART2 (8/10), I2C3 (3/5), I2S3 (M0: 12/13/35/38/40 asserted)
rows.cite: copper; wiring/cables.json

rows.item: run spk-hat — the CANNOT DETERMINE is now settled
rows.measurement: wiring/cables.json records the speaker pins as "SPK+, SPK- (codec line/HP out, or an amplifier: CANNOT DETERMINE)". THE COPPER SAYS AMPLIFIER: J1.1 <- C9/FB3 <- U1.16 (+OUT_R) and J1.2 <- C8/FB2 <- U1.14 (-OUT_R), i.e. the PAM8406D's bridged right channel through ferrites, not the codec's LINE_OUT. The codec's LEFT_LOP/RIGHT_LOP go to C1/C2 and into the amplifier inputs. That CANNOT DETERMINE can be retired, and the speaker sees a bridged 5 V class-D output, not a line level.
rows.cite: copper: U1, FB2, FB3, C8, C9, J1 pad->net

rows.item: run mic-hat — the model may carry a cable the robot has not got
rows.measurement: wiring/cables.json has a run "mic-hat" with cable_mm null and part:microduck-mic says the transducer, count, position and connector are all CANNOT DETERMINE. The copper shows the HAT carries its OWN mic: MK1, an LMA2718 MEMS part on +3V3, coupled through C10 into U2.16 (MIC2R/LINE2R, the pin Pollen's ALSA config calls Mic3R). Two Wago terminals J2 and J9 are ALSO wired to mic inputs with 10 k bias resistors to +5V. So "the head microphone" is either the on-board MK1 with no cable at all, or an external capsule on J2/J9 with one. Our model asserts the cable. WHAT SETTLES IT: a teardown photo of the HAT in the head showing whether anything is in J2 or J9.
rows.cite: copper: MK1, C10, U2.16, J2, J9, R22, R23; wiring/cables.json run mic-hat; part:microduck-mic uncertainties[0]

rows.item: run hat-radxa-40pin overstates the I2S by one pin
rows.measurement: The run records "I2S3 (M0: 12/13/35/38/40 asserted)". Header pin 13 is UNCONNECTED on the HAT — the copper marks it unconnected-(J4-Pin_13-Pad13) — because MCLK comes from Y1 on the board. The correct list is 12/35/38/40, and "asserted" becomes "measured". One pin in one string, but it is the difference between a reader wiring an MCLK and not.
rows.cite: copper J4 pad 13; wiring/cables.json run hat-radxa-40pin

rows.item: the servo chain branches at a board with an unknown port count
rows.measurement: The chain modelled in cables.json is hat -> id34 -> id33 -> id32 -> id31 -> id30 -> imu200 -> {id20, id10}: imu200 needs THREE bus connectors, one in and two out. An XL330 has exactly two, so the branch cannot be at a servo. part:microduck-imu-to-dxl already records the connector count as CANNOT DETERMINE and says the wiring lane put the branch there. Nothing has changed that. WHAT SETTLES IT: a photograph of the imu_to_dxl v2 board; its schematic is not published.
rows.cite: wiring/cables.json cables[]; ce-parts/microduck-imu-to-dxl/electrical.part.json uncertainties[0]

rows.item: every fitted active device on the HAT is on a rail
rows.measurement: 7 fitted active devices checked, every one has at least one pad on +BATT, +5V, +3V3 or +1V8.
rows.cite: copper

rows.item: off-board devices
rows.measurement: ToF -> J5.2 = +3V3. Camera -> the Radxa CSI connector pin 22 VCC_3V3, not the HAT. imu_to_dxl -> the servo bus VDD = +BATT. Speaker -> J1, driven, not powered. Mic -> either MK1 on +3V3 or a capsule on J2/J9 biased through 10 k from +5V. No modelled device is on no rail.
rows.cite: copper; part:imx219 / part:microduck-camera-module requires[VCC_3V3]

rows.item: the one function that is powered and has no software
rows.measurement: U11 BMI088 is fully powered (+3V3 through R9 0 R), addressed at 0x19/0x68, and its INT1 is routed to header pin 15 through R25 — and Pollen's runtime never reads it. The control IMU is the LSM6DSV16X on the imu_to_dxl board at Dynamixel ID 200 instead. That is the "two IMUs" the press mentions: one of them is dormant hardware, not a redundant sensor.
rows.cite: copper: U11, R9, R14, R15, R25; teardown §4 "Actually fitted, but unused by software"

rows.item: "Connector types on the HAT are CANNOT DETERMINE"
rows.measurement: J13/J14 = Dynamixel-3 (JST EH 2.5 mm, 3-pin, wired in PARALLEL — same GND, same +BATT, same data net); J3/J11 = Dynamixel-4 (JST EH 4-pin, RS-485, driven by U8 SIT3088E); J5-J8 = JST SH 1.0 mm 4-pin (Stemma/Qwiic); J1, J2, J9 = Wago-2 screwless terminals (speaker, and two external mic inputs); J4 = 2x20 SMD female header. AND THERE IS NO BATTERY INPUT CONNECTOR AT ALL — the pack arrives on a motor connector.  ||  OUR RECORD SAYS: part:microduck-robot-hat-pcb uncertainties[0]: "Connector types on the HAT (servo header, J5, battery input, speaker/mic) are CANNOT DETERMINE"  ||  CHANGE: replace the uncertainty with the measured connector list, and record that the battery input IS a motor connector.
rows.cite: ce-parts/microduck-robot-hat-pcb/electrical.part.json record.uncertainties[0] | copper: J1/J2/J3/J4/J5/J6/J7/J8/J9/J11/J13/J14 footprints and pad->net; README.md

rows.item: "Transceiver, regulators, fusing ... CANNOT DETERMINE"
rows.measurement: Transceiver: the TTL half-duplex path is discrete — U7 SN74LVC1G126 (non-inverting, active-high enable) drives the bus, U6 SN74LVC1G125 (active-low enable) and U5 74LVC1G08 return it, all three steered by one net, Dynamixel_dir, which is generated on the board by Q1 (MMBT3906) off the host TX line through R27 with R28 20 k to ground — a self-steering circuit with NO direction GPIO, exactly as the teardown deduced from the absence of one in the source. The RS-485 side is U8 SIT3088E on J3/J11. Regulators: U9 AP63205 (fixed 5.0 V, 2 A) with L4 6.8 uH, U3 XC6206P182MR (1.8 V from 3.3 V), U10 LM5050-1 + Q2 SI2312 as an ideal diode OR-ing the buck output with header 5 V. Fusing: TH1, a 100 R PTC thermistor, IS ON THE DATA LINE, not on power — the chain is transceiver -> R33 150 R -> D4 5V1 zener to ground -> TH1 -> J13/J14 pin 3. NFC reader: THERE IS NONE, in any of the 127 footprints.  ||  OUR RECORD SAYS: part:microduck-robot-hat-pcb uncertainties[1]: "Transceiver, regulators, fusing, NFC reader, REC LED: CANNOT DETERMINE"  ||  CHANGE: replace the uncertainty with the measured part list; delete the NFC reader from the open questions.
rows.cite: ce-parts/microduck-robot-hat-pcb/electrical.part.json record.uncertainties[1] | copper: U3, U5, U6, U7, U8, U9, U10, Q1, Q2, R27, R28, R33, TH1, D4, L4 pad->net

rows.item: the I2S3 mux was an assertion and is now a measurement
rows.measurement: M0, and pin 13 is NOT part of it. The HAT wires I2S to header pins 12, 35, 38 and 40 only. Pin 13 (I2S3_MCLK_M0) is explicitly unconnected; the codec's MCLK comes from Y1, a 12 MHz oscillator on the HAT. M1 is not merely unused, it is OCCUPIED: pins 19/21/23/24 are wired to the Stemma headers J7 and J8.  ||  OUR RECORD SAYS: part:microduck-robot-hat-pcb uncertainties[2] and part:radxa-zero-3w unknowns[4]: "I2S3 mux M0 (pins 12/13/35/38/40) vs M1 (19/21/23/24): the dts pinctrl was not read — the M0 pins are the wiring lane's assertion"  ||  CHANGE: record M0 as MEASURED, list the four pins 12/35/38/40, and state that MCLK is board-local.

At the pack top of 8.2 V that is 0.490 mA into the zener and 3.3 V at the pin. It is a logic battery-present line. No Pollen source read here uses it.  ||  OUR RECORD SAYS: nothing in this repo mentions it; the teardown says "There is no fuel gauge and no ADC", which is true and has been read as "the HAT tells the host nothing about the battery".  ||  CHANGE: add it to part:microduck-robot-hat-pcb as a provided signal, and to the HAT-to-Radxa run's pin list.

rows.item: which board revision this whole study is about
rows.measurement: Every connectivity statement here is read from rev C1 (clone commit 23eab119, "[added] Production file for C1"), the revision Pollen publishes production files for. out/pcb/hat/mesh-revision.json measured that the board in POLLEN'S OWN SIMULATION MESH is a different, pre-release layout (fbd885d, before "the 40-pin GPIO conn. is inverted"), whose Dynamixel connectors sit at the other end of the board. The connector POSITIONS were compared across four revisions; THE NETS WERE NOT. So "the servos are on +BATT" is proven for C1 and is corroborated for every revision by two revision-independent sources — the README ("designed to use of the motor connector as an power input") and Pollen's own runtime, which reads the pack voltage out of the servos' supply register and clears their input-voltage shutdown — but it is not proven pad-by-pad on fbd885d, A1 or B1. WHAT SETTLES IT: re-fetch the repository's git history and diff the +BATT net across the four revisions; out/pcb/hat/mesh-revision.json did exactly that for the drill table on 2026-09-04.
rows.cite: reference/pollen-elec-rpi-robot-hat/PROVENANCE.json clone_commit; out/pcb/hat/mesh-revision.json
